sents.t: On December 31st, Oakville was cold, but the town square was full of people.
Emma, Carlos, Lily, and I went there together at ten o’clock.
There was a big stage with a band, and people were dancing to keep warm.
“What are your New Year’s resolutions?” Emma asked.
“I’m going to get my driver’s license,” I said.
“And I’m going to go to the gym three times a week.”
“Everybody says that in January! I’m going to cook more and eat less fast food.”
“I’m going to finish my art portfolio,” Emma said.
“And I’m going to save money for a trip to Japan.”
At 11:59, everyone looked at the big clock on City Hall.
We started the countdown together: “Ten, nine, eight...” At midnight, everyone shouted, “Happy New Year!” Fireworks lit up the sky, and people hugged and kissed.
In my country, it was already morning.
“Happy New Year, Mom! This year is going to be great.”
